label: Electric kettle or toaster

questions.why: Kettles and toasters need different care.

questions.text: Does your water leave white marks in the kettle?
questions.why: Scale builds up on the heating plate.

questions.text: Is the kettle filled above the maximum line?
How often is the crumb tray emptied?
Is the power cord in good condition?
questions.why: Damaged cords are a shock and fire risk.

questions.text: Have you noticed it not switching off, a burning smell or sparks?
questions.why: Early signs let you get it checked before a small fault grows.

care_tips.text: Switch off and unplug the appliance before cleaning it.
care_tips.why: Cleaning an appliance that is plugged in risks an electric shock.

care_tips.text: Don't open the appliance yourself; leave repairs to the brand's authorised service.
care_tips.why: Inside there are live parts, and opening it can also end the warranty.

care_tips.text: Don't bypass or tamper with the thermostat or any safety cut-out.
care_tips.why: These stop the appliance overheating; without them it can cause burns or a fire.

care_tips.text: Stop using it if the cord is worn or damaged, and contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: Damaged cords can cause shocks and fires.

care_tips.text: Descale the kettle as the manual describes.
care_tips.why: Scale makes the heating plate work harder.

care_tips.text: Fill the kettle between the minimum and maximum lines.
Empty the toaster's crumb tray regularly (unplugged and cool).
If it does not switch off by itself or smells of burning, unplug it and contact the brand's service.
care_tips.why: The automatic cut-off may have failed.

reminders.text: Descale the kettle or empty the toaster's crumb tray (unplugged).
reminders.note: Check your manual for the interval for your model.
